Done. The verified solution is at **`~/NUMA_DRIFT_AUDIT_SOLUTION.md`** (the tested script is `~/numa_drift_audit.sh`; the embedded copy is byte-identical to the tested file).

## What was wrong / root cause
- `numa_maps` `Nx=` counts are **page-type-blind** (anonymous/file/shmem lumped per node), so per-node RSS cannot be split from it alone — it must be reconciled by VMA start address against `smaps` (`Anonymous`, `AnonHugePages`, `FilePmdMapped`, `ShmemPmdMapped`, `Shared_*`).
- `numa_maps` stores **no provenance**: migrated, THP-collapsed, and `mbind`-placed pages look identical in one read. Causes must be inferred from independent signals (`smaps` structure, `/proc/vmstat` deltas, VMA policy vs task default, parent policy).
- Reading `/proc/vmstat` perturbs it (the audit allocates memory), so counters cannot be in the "unchanged system" identity set — hence separate `snapshot` vs `counters` streams.

## Fix
A deterministic Bash auditor with four commands:
- `snapshot <pid>` — canonical, sorted, timestamp-free placement state (byte-identical reruns).
- `counters <pid>` — volatile global counters (used only as deltas).
- `audit <pid> [base.snap base.cnt]` — reconciliation + named-cause table, explicit `unknown:<why>` everywhere evidence is missing.
- `diff A B [A.cnt B.cnt]` — attributes placement and counter deltas (THP fault/khugepaged, autonuma vs explicit migration, KSM, THP split) and detects `mbind` policy changes.

## Verified
| Requirement | Result |
|---|---|
| RSS reconciles to `statm` ≤1% | `delta_pct=0% verdict=PASS` (215 MB target) |
| Every class named or explicit unknown | `mbind_override`, `unknown:no_baseline_counters`, `unknown_pagetypeinfo`, `unknown_thp_sysfs`, … |
| Consecutive runs byte-identical | `cmp` → `BYTE-IDENTICAL` (snapshot and no-baseline audit) |
| Reads numa_maps/status/smaps/pagetypeinfo | all parsed; unreadable sources surfaced as explicit unknowns |
| THP/khugepaged/migration/mbind/inherited policy attributed | dedicated buckets + diff attribution |

Validated with `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` (clean), on a container where `/proc/pagetypeinfo` and `/sys/kernel/mm` are deliberately unavailable, which exercised the explicit-unknown paths.

signatures.description: A long-running service starts with an explicit set_mempolicy MPOL_BIND binding yet its per-node RSS drifts over hours; write a bash audit that reads numa_maps, proc status, smaps and pagetypeinfo to attribute each migrated page to a named cause (transparent hugepage collapse, khugepaged, page migration, mbind override, inherited task policy). The catch: numa_maps reports N0/N1 hints but lumps shared-anonymous and file-backed pages together, so attribution must reconcile against smaps and detect policy overrides applied by other processes. Acceptance: per-node RSS reconciles to statm within 1 percent, every drift class carries a named reason or an explicit unknown, and consecutive runs on an unchanged system are byte-identical.
